title: Basic SVO Word Order (Subject + Verb + Object)
explanation: Standard Mandarin declarative sentences follow a strict Subject-Verb-Object order, similar to English. Unlike English, Mandarin verbs do not conjugate for person or tense.
example: 我喝咖啡。 (Wǒ hē kāfēi.)
example_translation: I drink coffee. / আমি কফি পান করি।

title: Time and Place Word Order
explanation: Time expressions and location phrases almost always appear before the verb, following the order Subject + Time + Place + Verb (+ Object). Time may also precede the subject for emphasis.
example: 我明天在家学习汉语。 (Wǒ míngtiān zài jiā xuéxí Hànyǔ.)
example_translation: I will study Chinese at home tomorrow. / আমি আগামীকাল বাড়িতে চাইনিজ শিখব।

title: Equational Sentences with 是 (shì)
explanation: Use 是 (shì) to link two nouns or noun phrases (A is B). Do not use 是 before standalone adjectives like 'happy' or 'tall'; use degree adverbs such as 很 instead.
example: 她是我的汉语老师。 (Tā shì wǒ de Hànyǔ lǎoshī.)
example_translation: She is my Chinese teacher. / তিনি আমার চাইনিজ শিক্ষক।

title: Possession and Existence with 有 (yǒu)
explanation: 有 (yǒu) expresses both possession ('to have') and existence ('there is/are' when preceded by a location). Its negation is always 没有 (méiyǒu), never 不有.
example: 桌子上有一本书。 (Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yī běn shū.)
example_translation: There is a book on the table. / টেবিলের উপর একটি বই আছে।

title: Location and Presence with 在 (zài)
explanation: As a main verb, 在 indicates where someone or something is located (Subject + 在 + Place). As a preposition, 在 + Place precedes the main verb to show where an action occurs.
example: 我的朋友在北京工作。 (Wǒ de péngyou zài Běijīng gōngzuò.)
example_translation: My friend works in Beijing. / আমার বন্ধু বেইজিংয়ে কাজ করে।

title: General Negation with 不 (bù)
explanation: Place 不 directly before verbs, modal verbs, or adjectives to negate present, future, or habitual actions and states. 不 changes tone to bú before fourth-tone syllables.
example: 我今天不去学校。 (Wǒ jīntiān bú qù xuéxiào.)
example_translation: I am not going to school today. / আমি আজ স্কুলে যাচ্ছি না।

title: Past and Possession Negation with 没 / 没有
explanation: Use 没 or 没有 before a verb to state that an action did not happen in the past, or to negate possession with 有. Never keep the completion particle 了 with 没.
example: 我昨天没有看电影。 (Wǒ zuótiān méiyǒu kàn diànyǐng.)
example_translation: I did not watch a movie yesterday. / আমি গতকাল সিনেমা দেখিনি।

title: Yes-No Questions with 吗 (ma)
explanation: Attach the neutral-tone particle 吗 to the end of any declarative statement to turn it into a yes-no question. The rest of the sentence order remains unchanged.
example: 你喜欢喝茶吗？ (Nǐ xǐhuan hē chá ma?)
example_translation: Do you like drinking tea? / তুমি কি চা খেতে পছন্দ করো?

title: Follow-Up and Location Questions with 呢 (ne)
explanation: 呢 is placed at the end of a noun phrase to bounce a question back ('And what about...?') or to ask where someone or something is. It can also mark an ongoing situation.
example: 我很好，你呢？ (Wǒ hěn hǎo, nǐ ne?)
example_translation: I am very well, and you? / আমি খুব ভালো আছি, আর তুমি?

title: Possessive and Attributive Particle 的 (de)
explanation: Place 的 between a modifier (possessor, adjective, or clause) and a noun to show possession or description. 的 is often omitted between pronouns and close family members.
example: 这是哥哥的电脑。 (Zhè shì gēge de diànnǎo.)
example_translation: This is my older brother's computer. / এটি বড় ভাইয়ের কম্পিউটার।

title: Adjectival Predicates with Degree Adverbs (很/太/真)
explanation: Adjectives functioning as predicates usually require a degree adverb like 很 (very, often neutral filler), 太 (too/extremely), or 真 (really). Without one, an adjective sounds comparative.
example: 今天天气很热。 (Jīntiān tiānqì hěn rè.)
example_translation: The weather is hot today. / আজ আবহাওয়া খুব গরম।

title: Asking Quantities with 几 (jǐ) vs. 多少 (duōshao)
explanation: Use 几 for small expected numbers (typically under 10) and always follow it with a measure word. Use 多少 for larger or unknown quantities, where the measure word is optional.
example: 你们班有多少个学生？ (Nǐmen bān yǒu duōshao gè xuésheng?)
example_translation: How many students are in your class? / তোমাদের ক্লাসে কতজন শিক্ষার্থী আছে?

title: In-Situ Question Words (谁/什么/哪/怎么)
explanation: Mandarin question words stay in the exact slot where the answer belongs rather than moving to the front of the sentence. Never combine them with the yes-no particle 吗.
example: 你星期天去哪里买水果？ (Nǐ xīngqītiān qù nǎlǐ mǎi shuǐguǒ?)
example_translation: Where are you going to buy fruit on Sunday? / তুমি রবিবার কোথায় ফল কিনতে যাবে?

title: Common Nominal Measure Words (个/本/张/件)
explanation: Numbers and demonstratives (这/那) require a measure word before a noun. 个 is general, 本 is for bound books, 张 is for flat objects like paper/tables, and 件 is for clothes/matters.
example: 我买了两本书和一件衣服。 (Wǒ mǎi le liǎng běn shū hé yī jiàn yīfu.)
example_translation: I bought two books and one piece of clothing. / আমি দুটি বই এবং একটি জামা কিনেছি।

title: Desires and Intentions with 想 (xiǎng) vs. 要 (yào)
explanation: 想 expresses a softer wish ('would like to'), whereas 要 conveys a stronger determination, need, or immediate plan ('want to / going to'). Their negative forms are 不想 and 不要/不想.
example: 我想买一张去上海的火车票。 (Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī zhāng qù Shànghǎi de huǒchēpiào.)
example_translation: I would like to buy a train ticket to Shanghai. / আমি সাংহাই যাওয়ার একটি ট্রেনের টিকিট কিনতে চাই।

title: Ability and Permission with 会 / 能 / 可以
explanation: 会 denotes a learned skill ('know how to'), 能 expresses physical ability or possibility ('be able to'), and 可以 indicates permission or suitability ('may / can').
example: 你会说汉语吗？这里可以坐吗？ (Nǐ huì shuō Hànyǔ ma? Zhèlǐ kěyǐ zuò ma?)
example_translation: Can you speak Chinese? May I sit here? / তুমি কি চাইনিজ বলতে পারো? এখানে কি বসা যাবে?

title: Completion and Change-of-State Particle 了 (le)
explanation: Placed right after a verb, 了 marks a completed action; placed at the end of a sentence, 了 signals a new situation or change of state. It is not a simple past-tense marker.
example: 下雨了，我买了一把伞。 (Xiàyǔ le, wǒ mǎi le yī bǎ sǎn.)
example_translation: It started raining, so I bought an umbrella. / বৃষ্টি শুরু হয়েছে, তাই আমি একটি ছাতা কিনেছি।

title: Counting and Measuring with 二 (èr) vs. 两 (liǎng)
explanation: Use 二 for counting, phone numbers, dates, and ordinal numbers (第二). Use 两 before measure words and large units like 百/千/万 when specifying a quantity of two.
example: 我有两个姐姐，住在二楼。 (Wǒ yǒu liǎng gè jiějie, zhù zài èr lóu.)
example_translation: I have two older sisters who live on the second floor. / আমার দুইজন বড় বোন আছে, তারা দ্বিতীয় তলায় থাকে।

title: Polite Requests with 请 (qǐng)
explanation: Place 请 at the start of an imperative sentence to mean 'please'. It can also function as a main verb meaning 'to invite' or 'to treat someone'.
example: 请坐，请喝水！ (Qǐng zuò, qǐng hē shuǐ!)
example_translation: Please sit down and please have some water! / দয়া করে বসুন, দয়া করে পানি পান করুন!

title: Connecting Nouns with 和 (hé)
explanation: 和 joins nouns, pronouns, or noun phrases ('and'), but never connects two separate clauses or sentences. Use commas or words like 而且 to join clauses.
example: 爸爸和妈妈都在医院工作。 (Bàba hé māma dōu zài yīyuàn gōngzuò.)
example_translation: Both Dad and Mom work at the hospital. / বাবা এবং মা দুজনেই হাসপাতালে কাজ করেন।

title: Suggestions and Soft Confirmation with 吧 (ba)
explanation: Attach 吧 to the end of a sentence to soften a command into a polite suggestion ('let's / why not') or to ask for confirmation when you already assume the answer.
example: 我们一起去吃晚饭吧！ (Wǒmen yīqǐ qù chī wǎnfàn ba!)
example_translation: Let's go eat dinner together! / চলো একসাথে রাতের খাবার খেতে যাই!

title: Exclamatory and Softening Particle 啊 (a)
explanation: Sentence-final 啊 adds warmth, surprise, urgency, or softening to statements, questions, and imperatives. Its pronunciation shifts slightly depending on the preceding vowel or consonant.
example: 这里的风景真美啊！ (Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng zhēn měi a!)
example_translation: The scenery here is truly beautiful! / এখানকার দৃশ্য সত্যিই অনেক সুন্দর!

title: Ongoing Actions with 正在 (zhèngzài)
explanation: Place 正在 (or 正/在 alone) before a verb to indicate an action in progress ('be doing right now'). Sentences with 正在 often end with 呢.
example: 他正在打电话呢，请等一下。 (Tā zhèngzài dǎ diànhuà ne, qǐng děng yīxià.)
example_translation: He is on the phone right now; please wait a moment. / তিনি এখন ফোনে কথা বলছেন, অনুগ্রহ করে একটু অপেক্ষা করুন।

title: Experiential Aspect with 过 (guò)
explanation: Place 过 immediately after a verb to indicate having experienced an action at least once in the past ('have ever done'). Negate it with 没/没有 while keeping 过.
example: 我去过三次长城。 (Wǒ qù guo sān cì Chángchéng.)
example_translation: I have been to the Great Wall three times. / আমি তিনবার মহাপ্রাচীরে গিয়েছি।

title: Continuous State Particle 着 (zhe)
explanation: Placed right after a verb, 着 shows that an action's resulting state continues ('is wearing', 'is open', 'is sitting'). It also links two verbs where the first describes the manner of the second.
example: 门开着，他笑着走进来。 (Mén kāi zhe, tā xiào zhe zǒu jìnlái.)
example_translation: The door is open, and he walks in smiling. / দরজা খোলা আছে, সে হাসতে হাসতে ভেতরে ঢুকছে।

title: Complement of Degree with 得 (de)
explanation: Use Verb + 得 + Adjective/Phrase to evaluate how well or to what degree an action is performed. If the verb takes an object, repeat the verb before 得 (V + O + V + 得 + Adj).
example: 她汉语说得非常流利。 (Tā Hànyǔ shuō de fēicháng liúlì.)
example_translation: She speaks Chinese very fluently. / তিনি খুব সাবলীলভাবে চাইনিজ বলেন।

title: Imminent Future with 快要…了 / 就要…了
explanation: Wrap a verb or adjective between 快要 (or 快/就要) and sentence-final 了 to say something is about to happen soon. Use 就要…了 when a specific time expression is stated.
example: 火车快要开了，我们快走吧。 (Huǒchē kuàiyào kāi le, wǒmen kuài zǒu ba.)
example_translation: The train is about to leave; let's hurry up. / ট্রেনটি শীঘ্রই ছেড়ে যাবে, চলো তাড়াতাড়ি যাই।

title: Comparisons of Superiority with 比 (bǐ)
explanation: Compare two items using A + 比 + B + Adjective. Never put 很 before the adjective; to show degree, add 一点儿, 得多, or 多了 after the adjective.
example: 今天比昨天冷得多。 (Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng de duō.)
example_translation: Today is much colder than yesterday. / আজ গতকালের চেয়ে অনেক বেশি ঠান্ডা।

title: Negative Comparisons with 没有 (méiyǒu)
explanation: Use A + 没有 + B + (那么) + Adjective to express 'A is not as [Adjective] as B'. It is the natural negative counterpart to 比 comparisons.
example: 弟弟没有哥哥那么高。 (Dìdi méiyǒu gēge nàme gāo.)
example_translation: The younger brother is not as tall as the older brother. / ছোট ভাই বড় ভাইয়ের মতো অত লম্বা নয়।

title: Expressing Sameness with 跟…一样
explanation: Use A + 跟/和 + B + 一样 (+ Adjective) to say two things are the same or share the same quality. Insert 不 before 一样 to say they are different.
example: 这双鞋跟那双一样贵。 (Zhè shuāng xié gēn nà shuāng yīyàng guì.)
example_translation: This pair of shoes is as expensive as that pair. / এই জোড়া জুতো ওই জোড়ার মতোই দামি।

title: Verbal Measure Words (次/遍/趟)
explanation: Count actions by placing Number + Verbal Measure Word after the verb: 次 counts occurrences, 遍 emphasizes doing something from start to finish, and 趟 counts round trips.
example: 这本书我已经看了两遍，还要再去一趟书店。 (Zhè běn shū wǒ yǐjīng kàn le liǎng biàn, hái yào zài qù yī tàng shūdiàn.)
example_translation: I have already read this book twice from cover to cover, and I still need to make a trip to the bookstore. / আমি এই বইটি ইতিমধ্যে দুইবার পুরোটা পড়েছি, আর আমাকে আরও একবার বইয়ের দোকানে যেতে হবে।

title: Emphasizing Past Details with 是…的
explanation: Frame a known past event with 是…的 to emphasize when, where, how, or by whom it happened. Place the emphasized detail right after 是, and put 的 at the end (or before the object).
example: 我是坐飞机来中国的。 (Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái Zhōngguó de.)
example_translation: I came to China by plane. / আমি বিমানে চড়ে চীনে এসেছি।

title: Concessive Clauses with 虽然…但是…
explanation: Use 虽然 (although) in the first clause and 但是 or 可是 (but) in the second to express contrast. Unlike English, Mandarin regularly uses both conjunctions in the same sentence.
example: 虽然他很累，但是还在继续工作。 (Suīrán tā hěn lèi, dànshì hái zài jìxù gōngzuò.)
example_translation: Although he is very tired, he is still continuing to work. / যদিও সে খুব ক্লান্ত, তবুও সে কাজ চালিয়ে যাচ্ছে।

title: Cause and Effect with 因为…所以…
explanation: Introduce a reason with 因为 (because) and the resulting consequence with 所以 (so/therefore). Both words commonly appear together in Mandarin.
example: 因为道路结冰，所以我晚到了。 (Yīnwèi dàolù jiébīng, suǒyǐ wǒ wǎn dào le.)
example_translation: Because the road was icy, I arrived late. / রাস্তা বরফে জমে যাওয়ার কারণে আমি দেরিতে পৌঁছেছি।

title: Conditional Sentences with 如果/要是…就…
explanation: Begin a hypothetical condition with 如果 or 要是 ('if') and introduce the outcome with 就 ('then') before the verb of the main clause.
example: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去爬山了。 (Rúguǒ míngtiān xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù páshān le.)
example_translation: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go hiking. / যদি আগামীকাল বৃষ্টি হয়, তাহলে আমরা পাহাড়ে চড়তে যাব না।

title: Expressing 'Or' with 还是 (háishi) vs. 或者 (huòzhě)
explanation: Use 还是 to offer choices in questions ('A or B?'), and use 或者 to express alternatives in declarative statements. 还是 can also appear in embedded indirect questions.
example: 你喝咖啡还是喝茶？周末我或者看书，或者游泳。 (Nǐ hē kāfēi háishi hē chá? Zhōumò wǒ huòzhě kànshū, huòzhě yóuyǒng.)
example_translation: Do you drink coffee or tea? On weekends I either read or swim. / আপনি কফি পান করবেন নাকি চা? সপ্তাহান্তে আমি হয় বই পড়ি, নয়তো সাঁতার কাটি।

title: Repetition in Future vs. Past with 再 (zài) vs. 又 (yòu)
explanation: Both mean 'again', but 再 refers to a planned or future repetition, while 又 refers to an action that has already happened again (or occurs cyclically).
example: 昨天他迟到了，今天他又迟到了，希望明天别再迟到了。 (Zuótiān tā chídào le, jīntiān tā yòu chídào le, xīwàng míngtiān bié zài chídào le.)
example_translation: Yesterday he was late, today he was late again; I hope he won't be late again tomorrow. / গতকাল সে দেরি করেছিল, আজ সে আবার দেরি করেছে; আশা করি আগামীকাল আর দেরি করবে না।

title: Negative Imperatives with 别 (bié) / 不要 (búyào)
explanation: Place 别 or 不要 before a verb to tell someone not to do something ('don't'). 别 is more concise and conversational, while 不要 can sound firmer.
example: 别忘了带护照和手机。 (Bié wàng le dài hùzhào hé shǒujī.)
example_translation: Don't forget to bring your passport and phone. / পাসপোর্ট ও মোবাইল ফোন আনতে ভুলো না।

title: Disposal Construction with 把 (bǎ)
explanation: Use Subject + 把 + Definite Object + Verb + Other Element (了/complement/location) to highlight how an action handles, moves, or changes a specific object. The verb cannot stand bare.
example: 请把空调打开，把窗户关上。 (Qǐng bǎ kōngtiáo dǎkāi, bǎ chuānghu guānshàng.)
example_translation: Please turn on the air conditioner and close the window. / অনুগ্রহ করে এয়ার কন্ডিশনারটি চালু করুন এবং জানালাটি বন্ধ করুন।

title: Passive Voice with 被 / 叫 / 让
explanation: Form passives using Receiver + 被 (+ Doer) + Verb + Result/了. In spoken Mandarin, 叫 and 让 also serve as passive markers, though they always require an explicit doer.
example: 我的自行车被小偷偷走了。 (Wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi xiǎotōu tōu zǒu le.)
example_translation: My bicycle was stolen by a thief. / আমার সাইকেলটি চোর চুরি করে নিয়ে গেছে।

title: Adverbial Manner Marker 地 (de)
explanation: Place 地 between an adjective (often reduplicated or paired with 很/非常) and a verb to turn the adjective into an adverb describing how the action is performed.
example: 孩子们高高兴兴地跑进了教室。 (Háizimen gāogāoxìngxìng de pǎo jìn le jiàoshì.)
example_translation: The children ran happily into the classroom. / শিশুরা খুশি মনে দৌড়ে শ্রেণিকক্ষে ঢুকল।

title: Progressive Change with 越来越 (yuèláiyuè)
explanation: Place 越来越 before an adjective or mental verb to express a continuous increase over time ('more and more'). Do not add 很 before the adjective.
example: 他的汉语水平越来越高了。 (Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng yuèláiyuè gāo le.)
example_translation: His Chinese proficiency is getting higher and higher. / তার চাইনিজ ভাষার দক্ষতা দিন দিন আরও ভালো হচ্ছে।

title: Correlative Increase with 越…越…
explanation: Use 越 + A + 越 + B ('the more A, the more B') to show that B changes in direct proportion to A. Both clauses may share a subject or have different subjects.
example: 风越刮越大，雨也越下越急。 (Fēng yuè guā yuè dà, yǔ yě yuè xià yuè jí.)
example_translation: The harder the wind blows, the heavier the rain falls. / বাতাস যত জোরে বইছে, বৃষ্টিও তত প্রবলভাবে পড়ছে।

title: Simultaneous Actions with 一边…一边…
explanation: Use 一边 + Verb 1 + 一边 + Verb 2 to show a single subject performing two active actions at the exact same time ('while doing A, also doing B').
example: 他喜欢一边听音乐，一边做作业。 (Tā xǐhuan yībiān tīng yīnyuè, yībiān zuò zuòyè.)
example_translation: He likes listening to music while doing homework. / সে গান শুনতে শুনতে বাড়ির কাজ করতে পছন্দ করে।

title: Co-occurring Qualities with 又…又…
explanation: Link two adjectives or stative verbs with 又 + A + 又 + B ('both A and B') to show they exist together. Both items should match in positive or negative tone.
example: 这家餐厅的菜又便宜又好吃。 (Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài yòu piányi yòu hǎochī.)
example_translation: The food at this restaurant is both cheap and delicious. / এই রেস্তোরাঁর খাবার সস্তা এবং সুস্বাদু উভয়ই।

title: Progressive Addition with 不但…而且…
explanation: Use 不但…而且… ('not only... but also...') to add a stronger or further point. If both clauses share the same subject, place the subject before 不但; if subjects differ, put 不但 first.
example: 她不但会说英语，而且汉语也说得很棒。 (Tā búdàn huì shuō Yīngyǔ, érqiě Hànyǔ yě shuō de hěn bàng.)
example_translation: She not only speaks English, but also speaks Chinese wonderfully. / সে শুধু ইংরেজিই বলতে পারে না, বরং চমৎকার চাইনিজও বলে।

title: Exclusion and Inclusion with 除了…以外
explanation: 除了 X (以外) means 'except X' when the main clause uses 都 ('all'), and 'besides/in addition to X' when the main clause uses 还 or 也 ('also').
example: 除了小王以外，大家都到了。 (Chúle Xiǎo Wáng yǐwài, dàjiā dōu dào le.)
example_translation: Everyone has arrived except Xiao Wang. / শিয়াও ওয়াং ছাড়া সবাই পৌঁছে গেছে।

title: Immediate Sequence with 一…就…
explanation: Use 一 + Action 1 + 就 + Action 2 to indicate that the second event follows immediately upon the first ('as soon as...'). It works for both past sequences and general habits.
example: 我一到家就给你发短信。 (Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù gěi nǐ fā duǎnxìn.)
example_translation: I will text you as soon as I get home. / আমি বাড়ি পৌঁছানোমাত্রই তোমাকে মেসেজ করব।

title: Recent Past: 刚 (gāng) vs. 刚才 (gāngcái)
explanation: 刚 is an adverb meaning 'just now' and sits strictly after the subject and before the verb. 刚才 is a time noun meaning 'a moment ago' and can sit before or after the subject.
example: 刚才谁来了？我刚泡好茶。 (Gāngcái shéi lái le? Wǒ gāng pào hǎo chá.)
example_translation: Who came a moment ago? I just brewed the tea. / একটু আগে কে এসেছিল? আমি এইমাত্র চা বানিয়েছি।

title: Earliness vs. Lateness with 就 (jiù) vs. 才 (cái)
explanation: 就 before a verb signals that an action happened earlier, faster, or more easily than expected; 才 signals that it happened later, slower, or with difficulty (and usually drops 了).
example: 他八点就到了，我九点半才到。 (Tā bā diǎn jiù dào le, wǒ jiǔ diǎn bàn cái dào.)
example_translation: He arrived as early as eight, while I didn't arrive until nine-thirty. / সে আটটার আগেই পৌঁছে গিয়েছিল, আর আমি সাড়ে নয়টায় পৌঁছালাম।

title: Directional Complements (出来/进去/下来/起来)
explanation: Attach directional verbs like 出来 (out toward speaker), 进去 (in away from speaker), 下来 (down/stabilize), or 起来 (up/start) after a verb to show motion or figurative aspect.
example: 请你把笔记本拿出来，然后坐下来听课。 (Qǐng nǐ bǎ bǐjìběn ná chūlái, ránhòu zuò xiàlái tīngkè.)
example_translation: Please take out your notebook and then sit down to listen to the class. / অনুগ্রহ করে আপনার নোটবুকটি বের করুন এবং তারপর বসে ক্লাস শুনুন।

title: Resultative Complements (看懂/听见/做完/买到)
explanation: Combine an action verb directly with a result verb or adjective (e.g., 看懂 understand by reading, 听见 hear, 做完 finish doing, 买到 succeed in buying) to show the outcome.
example: 我听见有人敲门，但没看懂那张纸条。 (Wǒ tīngjiàn yǒu rén qiāo mén, dàn méi kàndǒng nà zhāng zhǐtiáo.)
example_translation: I heard someone knocking on the door, but I couldn't understand that note. / আমি শুনতে পেলাম কেউ দরজায় কড়া নাড়ছে, কিন্তু ওই চিরকুটটি বুঝতে পারিনি।

title: Potential Complements (买不到/看得懂/受不了)
explanation: Insert 得 (can) or 不 (cannot) between a verb and its result/directional complement to express feasibility, such as 买不到 (cannot buy), 看得懂 (can understand), or 受不了 (cannot bear).
example: 太晚了，现在肯定买不到票了，真让人受不了。 (Tài wǎn le, xiànzài kěndìng mǎi bú dào piào le, zhēn ràng rén shòubuliǎo.)
example_translation: It's too late—we definitely won't be able to buy tickets now, which is unbearable. / অনেক দেরি হয়ে গেছে, এখন নিশ্চিতভাবে টিকিট কেনা যাবে না, যা সত্যিই অসহনীয়।

title: Having Enough Time with 来得及 / 来不及
explanation: Use the fixed potential complements 来得及 ('there is still time to') and 来不及 ('it's too late to') either alone or right before a verb phrase.
example: 快出发吧，不然就来不及赶上飞机了！ (Kuài chūfā ba, bùrán jiù láibují gǎnshàng fēijī le!)
example_translation: Let's leave right away, otherwise it will be too late to catch the flight! / তাড়াতাড়ি রওনা হও, নাহলে ফ্লাইট ধরার আর সময় থাকবে না!

title: Verb Reduplication (AA / ABAB) for Casual Action
explanation: Reduplicate monosyllabic verbs (看看, 试试) or disyllabic verbs (休息休息) to soften the tone, meaning 'do briefly' or 'give it a try'. You can also insert 一 (看一看).
example: 你先休息休息，有空再看看这份报告。 (Nǐ xiān xiūxi xiūxi, yǒukòng zài kànkan zhè fèn bàogào.)
example_translation: Rest for a bit first, and take a look at this report when you have time. / আপনি আগে একটু বিশ্রাম নিন, সময় হলে এই প্রতিবেদনটি একটু দেখে নেবেন।

title: Prepositions 对 / 对于 / 关于
explanation: 对 introduces the target of an action or attitude ('toward/to'); 对于 introduces a topic of perspective ('as for/regarding'); 关于 means 'about/concerning' and often modifies nouns or starts a sentence.
example: 关于这个问题，大家对他的建议都很满意。 (Guānyú zhège wèntí, dàjiā duì tā de jiànyì dōu hěn mǎnyì.)
example_translation: Regarding this issue, everyone is very satisfied with his suggestion. / এই বিষয়ে, সবাই তার পরামর্শে খুবই সন্তুষ্ট।

title: Sequential Actions with 先…再…然后…
explanation: Order multiple steps logically using 先 (first), 再 or 然后 (then/next), and optionally 最后 (finally). Each marker sits before the verb of its clause.
example: 先洗手，再吃饭，然后去散步。 (Xiān xǐshǒu, zài chīfàn, ránhòu qù sànbù.)
example_translation: Wash your hands first, then eat, and then go for a walk. / আগে হাত ধোও, তারপর খাও, এবং এরপর হাঁটতে যাও।

title: Contrastive Correction with 不是…而是…
explanation: Use 不是 A，而是 B ('not A, rather B') to reject a mistaken assumption and immediately supply the true explanation.
example: 我不是不想去，而是实在没有时间。 (Wǒ bú shì bù xiǎng qù, érshì shízài méiyǒu shíjiān.)
example_translation: It's not that I don't want to go, but rather that I truly have no time. / এমন নয় যে আমি যেতে চাই না, বরং সত্যিই আমার কোনো সময় নেই।

title: Sufficient Condition with 只要…就…
explanation: Use 只要 + Condition + 就 + Result ('as long as..., then...') to express that one condition is enough to guarantee the outcome.
example: 只要坚持每天练习，你的口语就会进步。 (Zhǐyào jiānchí měitiān liànxí, nǐ de kǒuyǔ jiù huì jìnbù.)
example_translation: As long as you keep practicing every day, your speaking will improve. / যতদিন আপনি প্রতিদিন অনুশীলন চালিয়ে যাবেন, আপনার কথা বলার দক্ষতা উন্নত হবে।

title: Necessary Condition with 只有…才…
explanation: Use 只有 + Condition + 才 + Result ('only if..., then...') to emphasize that the stated condition is the sole indispensable requirement.
example: 只有通过考试，才能拿到毕业证书。 (Zhǐyǒu tōngguò kǎoshì, cái néng nádào bìyè zhèngshū.)
example_translation: Only by passing the exam can you obtain the graduation certificate. / কেবল পরীক্ষায় উত্তীর্ণ হলেই আপনি স্নাতক সনদপত্র পেতে পারেন।

title: Unconditional Statements with 无论/不管…都…
explanation: Follow 无论 or 不管 ('no matter') with an alternative (A还是B) or question word (怎么/什么/多么), paired with 都 or 也 in the main clause to show the result never changes.
example: 无论遇到什么困难，我们都要勇敢面对。 (Wúlùn yùdào shénme kùnnan, wǒmen dōu yào yǒnggǎn miànduì.)
example_translation: No matter what difficulties we encounter, we must face them bravely. / যত বাধাই আসুক না কেন, আমাদের সাহসের সাথে তার মোকাবিলা করতে হবে।

title: Known-Premise Deduction with 既然…就…
explanation: Use 既然 ('since / now that') to cite an already established fact, followed by 就 ('then') to draw a logical decision or suggestion from it.
example: 既然大家都同意了，那我们就按计划执行吧。 (Jìrán dàjiā dōu tóngyì le, nà wǒmen jiù àn jìhuà zhíxíng ba.)
example_translation: Since everyone agrees, let's carry it out according to the plan. / যেহেতু সবাই রাজি হয়েছে, তাহলে চলুন আমরা পরিকল্পনা অনুযায়ী কাজ করি।

title: Emphatic 'Even' with 连…都/也…
explanation: Highlight an extreme or unexpected example using 连 + Element + 都/也 + Verb/Adjective ('even X...'). It works in both positive and negative sentences.
example: 他忙得连午饭都忘了吃。 (Tā máng de lián wǔfàn dōu wàng le chī.)
example_translation: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat lunch. / সে এতটাই ব্যস্ত ছিল যে দুপুরের খাবার খেতেও ভুলে গিয়েছিল।

title: Hypothetical Concession with 即使…也…
explanation: Use 即使…也… ('even if...') to concede an extreme or hypothetical situation while asserting that the main outcome remains unchanged.
example: 即使明天刮大风，比赛也会按时举行。 (Jíshǐ míngtiān guā dàfēng, bǐsài yě huì ànshí jǔxíng.)
example_translation: Even if strong winds blow tomorrow, the match will still be held on time. / আগামীকাল প্রবল বাতাস বইলেও খেলাটি সময়মতো অনুষ্ঠিত হবে।

title: Factual Concession with 尽管…还是…
explanation: Unlike 即使 (hypothetical), 尽管 introduces an actual fact ('even though / despite'), and the second clause often uses 还是 or 仍然 ('still').
example: 尽管已经半夜了，办公室里还是灯火通明。 (Jǐnguǎn yǐjīng bànyè le, bàngōngshì lǐ háishi dēnghuǒ tōngmíng.)
example_translation: Even though it is already midnight, the office is still brightly lit. / যদিও ইতিমধ্যেই মধ্যরাত হয়ে গেছে, তবুও অফিসটি এখনও উজ্জ্বল আলোয় আলোকিত।

title: Escalating Addition with 不仅…还…
explanation: 不仅…还… (or 不仅…而且…) works like 不但…而且… ('not only... but also...'), and is slightly more formal and common in writing and speeches.
example: 阅读不仅能增长知识，还能开阔眼界。 (Yuèdú bùjǐn néng zēngzhǎng zhīshi, hái néng kāikuò yǎnjiè.)
example_translation: Reading can not only increase knowledge, but also broaden one's horizons. / পড়াশোনা কেবল জ্ঞানই বাড়ায় না, বরং দৃষ্টিভঙ্গিও প্রসারিত করে।

title: Balanced Dual Qualities with 既…又…
explanation: 既…又… ('both... and...') joins two parallel verbs or adjectives of equal weight, offering a slightly more formal and balanced tone than 又…又….
example: 这种新材料既轻便又耐用。 (Zhè zhǒng xīn cáiliào jì qīngbiàn yòu nàiyòng.)
example_translation: This new material is both lightweight and durable. / এই নতুন উপাদানটি হালকা এবং টেকসই উভয়ই।

title: Following Standards with 按 / 按照
explanation: The prepositions 按 and 按照 ('according to / in accordance with') introduce a rule, plan, or standard before the main verb. 按照 is slightly more formal and takes longer noun phrases.
example: 请按照说明书的步骤安装设备。 (Qǐng ànzhào shuōmíngshū de bùzhòu ānzhuāng shèbèi.)
example_translation: Please install the equipment according to the steps in the manual. / অনুগ্রহ করে নির্দেশিকার ধাপগুলো অনুসরণ করে যন্ত্রটি স্থাপন করুন।

title: Means and Method with 通过 (tōngguò)
explanation: As a preposition, 通过 + Noun/Verb Phrase means 'by means of / through', introducing the method or process by which a result is achieved.
example: 通过半年多的努力，他终于掌握了这门技术。 (Tōngguò bànnián duō de nǔlì, tā zhōngyú zhǎngwò le zhè mén jìshù.)
example_translation: Through more than half a year of hard work, he finally mastered this skill. / ছয় মাসেরও বেশি কঠোর পরিশ্রমের মাধ্যমে তিনি অবশেষে এই দক্ষতা অর্জন করেছেন।

title: Concurrent Change with 随着 (suízhe)
explanation: 随着 + Noun/Verb Phrase ('along with / as...') introduces a changing condition that causes or accompanies a parallel development in the main clause.
example: 随着科技的发展，人们的生活越来越方便。 (Suízhe kējì de fāzhǎn, rénmen de shēnghuó yuèláiyuè fāngbiàn.)
example_translation: With the development of technology, people's lives are becoming more and more convenient. / প্রযুক্তির উন্নতির সাথে সাথে মানুষের জীবন আরও বেশি সুবিধাজনক হয়ে উঠছে।

title: Appearance and Conjecture with 似乎 / 好像
explanation: Use 似乎 or 好像 before a verb or clause to say 'it seems / looks like'. 好像 is conversational and can pair with 似的 at the end; 似乎 is slightly more literary.
example: 他今天好像不太高兴，似乎有什么心事。 (Tā jīntiān hǎoxiàng bú tài gāoxìng, sìhū yǒu shénme xīnshì.)
example_translation: He doesn't seem very happy today; it looks like he has something on his mind. / আজ তাকে খুব একটা খুশি মনে হচ্ছে না, যেন তার মনে কোনো দুশ্চিন্তা আছে।

title: Unexpected Outcomes with 竟然 / 居然
explanation: Place 竟然 or 居然 before the predicate to express surprise that something happened contrary to expectation ('unexpectedly / actually').
example: 这么难的题，他竟然十分钟就解出来了！ (Zhème nán de tí, tā jìngrán shí fēnzhōng jiù jiě chūlái le!)
example_translation: Such a hard problem—and he actually solved it in just ten minutes! / এত কঠিন একটি অঙ্ক, অথচ সে মাত্র দশ মিনিটেই সমাধান করে ফেলল!

title: Rhetorical Questions with 难道 (nándào)
explanation: 难道 ('could it be that...? / surely...?') turns a statement into a rhetorical question implying the opposite is obviously true. It frequently pairs with 吗 at the end.
example: 难道你连这么简单的道理都不懂吗？ (Nándào nǐ lián zhème jiǎndān de dàolǐ dōu bù dǒng ma?)
example_translation: Don't you even understand such a simple principle? / তুমি কি এত সহজ একটা কথাও বোঝো না?

title: Contrary Result with 反而 (fǎn'ér)
explanation: Place 反而 ('instead / on the contrary') in the second clause when an action produces the exact opposite result of what was expected or intended.
example: 吃了药以后，他的头不但没好，反而更疼了。 (Chī le yào yǐhòu, tā de tóu búdàn méi hǎo, fǎn'ér gèng téng le.)
example_translation: After taking the medicine, his headache not only didn't improve, it actually got worse. / ওষুধ খাওয়ার পর তার মাথাব্যথা কমার বদলে উল্টো আরও বেড়ে গেল।

title: Warning of Consequences with 否则 / 不然
explanation: Use 否则 (formal) or 不然 (conversational) between two clauses to mean 'otherwise / or else', introducing the negative consequence if the first clause is not met.
example: 你必须抓紧时间，否则会错过最后期限。 (Nǐ bìxū zhuājǐn shíjiān, fǒuzé huì cuòguò zuìhòu qīxiàn.)
example_translation: You must hurry up; otherwise you will miss the deadline. / তোমাকে সময়ের সদ্ব্যবহার করতে হবে, নাহলে শেষ সময়সীমা পেরিয়ে যাবে।

title: Sequential Consequence with 于是 (yúshì)
explanation: 于是 ('so / thereupon / as a result') links a preceding situation to a natural action or event that immediately follows because of it.
example: 外面突然下起了大雨，于是大家决定改天再去。 (Wàimiàn tūrán xià qǐ le dàyǔ, yúshì dàjiā juédìng gǎitiān zài qù.)
example_translation: It suddenly started pouring outside, so everyone decided to go another day. / বাইরে হঠাৎ প্রবল বৃষ্টি শুরু হওয়ায় সবাই অন্য একদিন যাওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত নিল।

title: Fortunate Circumstances with 幸亏 (xìngkuī)
explanation: Use 幸亏 ('fortunately / luckily') at the beginning of a sentence or before the verb to show relief that a favorable factor prevented a bad outcome.
example: 幸亏带了雨伞，不然刚才就被淋湿了。 (Xìngkuī dài le yǔsǎn, bùrán gāngcái jiù bèi línshī le.)
example_translation: Luckily I brought an umbrella, otherwise I would have gotten soaked just now. / ভাগ্যিস ছাতা নিয়ে এসেছিলাম, নাহলে একটু আগেই বৃষ্টিতে ভিজে যেতাম।

title: Habitual Patterns with 往往 vs. 常常
explanation: 常常 simply means 'often' and can apply to past, future, or commands. 往往 means 'usually / tend to' and specifically describes a regular pattern tied to a stated condition.
example: 我常常去图书馆，周末那里往往坐满了人。 (Wǒ chángcháng qù túshūguǎn, zhōumò nàlǐ wǎngwǎng zuòmǎn le rén.)
example_translation: I often go to the library, and on weekends it tends to be packed with people. / আমি প্রায়ই লাইব্রেরিতে যাই, আর সপ্তাহান্তে সেখানে সাধারণত মানুষে ভরা থাকে।

title: Urgent Advice and Warnings with 千万 (qiānwàn)
explanation: 千万 ('be sure to / by all means') strengthens imperatives, especially negative warnings with 别/不要 ('whatever you do, don't...'). Never use it in plain past descriptions.
example: 开车的时候千万别看手机！ (Kāichē de shíhou qiānwàn bié kàn shǒujī!)
example_translation: Whatever you do, don't look at your phone while driving! / গাড়ি চালানোর সময় ভুলেও ফোনের দিকে তাকাবেন না!

title: Escalating Emphasis with 甚至 (shènzhì)
explanation: 甚至 ('even / to the point that') introduces an extreme example that goes beyond what was previously stated, highlighting degree or scope.
example: 他非常热爱音乐，甚至连吃饭时都在听交响乐。 (Tā fēicháng rè'ài yīnyuè, shènzhì lián chīfàn shí dōu zài tīng jiāoxiǎngyuè.)
example_translation: He loves music deeply—he even listens to symphonies while eating. / তিনি সংগীতকে ভীষণ ভালোবাসেন, এমনকি খাওয়ার সময়ও সিম্ফনি শোনেন।

title: Singling Out 'Especially' with 尤其 (yóuqí)
explanation: Use 尤其 ('especially / particularly') after a general statement to emphasize one standout subgroup or detail. It can precede 是, verbs, or adjectives.
example: 我喜欢运动，尤其是游泳和羽毛球。 (Wǒ xǐhuan yùndòng, yóuqí shì yóuyǒng hé yǔmáoqiú.)
example_translation: I like sports, especially swimming and badminton. / আমি খেলাধুলা পছন্দ করি, বিশেষ করে সাঁতার এবং ব্যাডমিন্টন।

title: Choosing the Lesser Evil with 宁可…也不…
explanation: Use 宁可 + Choice A + 也不 + Choice B ('would rather A than B') when both options are undesirable, showing firm preference for A.
example: 她宁可自己多加班，也不愿意随便敷衍客户。 (Tā nìngkě zìjǐ duō jiābān, yě bú yuànyì suíbiàn fūyǎn kèhù.)
example_translation: She would rather work extra overtime herself than carelessly brush off a client. / তিনি বরং নিজে অতিরিক্ত ওভারটাইম করবেন, তবুও গ্রাহকের সাথে অবহেলা করতে রাজি নন।

title: Preference Comparison with 与其…不如…
explanation: Use 与其 + Option A + 不如 + Option B ('rather than A, it is better to B') to advise choosing Option B over a less effective Option A.
example: 与其在这里抱怨，不如马上想办法解决。 (Yǔqí zài zhèlǐ bàoyuàn, bùrú mǎshàng xiǎng bànfǎ jiějué.)
example_translation: Rather than complaining here, it's better to find a way to solve it right away. / এখানে বসে অভিযোগ করার চেয়ে এখনই সমাধানের উপায় খোঁজা ভালো।

title: Extreme Hypothetical Concession with 哪怕…也…
explanation: 哪怕…也… ('even if...') concedes a particularly extreme or unlikely scenario, often conveying stronger determination than 即使.
example: 哪怕只有百分之一的希望，我们也要全力以赴。 (Nǎpà zhǐyǒu bǎifēn zhī yī de xīwàng, wǒmen yě yào quánlì yǐfù.)
example_translation: Even if there is only a one-percent hope, we will still give it our all. / এক শতাংশ আশা থাকলেও আমাদের সর্বাত্মক চেষ্টা করতে হবে।

title: A Fortiori 'Let Alone' with 何况 (hékuàng)
explanation: 何况 (often 更何况) follows an already strong point to argue that a second case is even more obvious ('let alone / all the more so'), frequently ending in a rhetorical question.
example: 连成年人都觉得难，何况是个孩子呢？ (Lián chéngniánrén dōu juéde nán, hékuàng shì gè háizi ne?)
example_translation: Even adults find it difficult, let alone a child! / প্রাপ্তবয়স্কদের কাছেই এটা কঠিন মনে হয়, সেখানে একটা বাচ্চার কথা তো বাদই দিলাম!

title: Preventing Bad Outcomes with 以免 / 省得
explanation: Place 以免 (formal) or 省得 (colloquial) before a second clause to mean 'in order to avoid / lest', explaining why the precautionary action in the first clause is taken.
example: 出门前再检查一遍，以免把重要文件落在家。 (Chūmén qián zài jiǎnchá yībiàn, yǐmiǎn bǎ zhòngyào wénjiàn là zài jiā.)
example_translation: Check once more before heading out so as to avoid leaving important documents at home. / বের হওয়ার আগে আরেকবার দেখে নাও, যাতে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কাগজপত্র বাড়িতে ভুলে না যাও।

title: Expressing Purpose with 以便 (yǐbiàn)
explanation: Use 以便 ('so that / in order to facilitate') between two clauses to show that the first action creates favorable conditions for the second.
example: 请提前提交申请，以便我们及时安排面试。 (Qǐng tíqián tíjiāo shēnqǐng, yǐbiàn wǒmen jíshí ānpái miànshì.)
example_translation: Please submit your application in advance so that we can arrange the interview promptly. / অনুগ্রহ করে আগেভাগে আবেদন জমা দিন, যাতে আমরা সময়মতো সাক্ষাৎকারের ব্যবস্থা করতে পারি।

title: Causal Progression with 从而 (cóng'ér)
explanation: 从而 ('thereby / thus') introduces a positive or logical outcome achieved directly through the action or method described in the preceding clause.
example: 公司改进了生产流程，从而大幅降低了成本。 (Gōngsī gǎijìn le shēngchǎn liúchéng, cóng'ér dàfú jiàngdī le chéngběn.)
example_translation: The company improved its production workflow, thereby significantly reducing costs. / কোম্পানিটি তাদের উৎপাদন প্রক্রিয়া উন্নত করেছে, যার ফলে খরচ উল্লেখযোগ্যভাবে কমেছে।

title: Summarizing Conclusions with 总之 (zǒngzhī)
explanation: Place 总之 ('in short / in summary') at the beginning of a concluding sentence to wrap up multiple details into one clear takeaway.
example: 虽然过程有些波折，但总之结果还是令人满意的。 (Suīrán guòchéng yǒuxiē bōzhé, dàn zǒngzhī jiéguǒ háishi lìng rén mǎnyì de.)
example_translation: Although the process had some twists and turns, in short, the result is still satisfying. / প্রক্রিয়াটিতে কিছুটা উত্থান-পতন থাকলেও সংক্ষেপে বলতে গেলে ফলাফলটি সন্তোষজনক।

title: Core Reason 'After All' with 毕竟 (bìjìng)
explanation: 毕竟 ('after all') introduces an undeniable, fundamental fact that explains or excuses the situation just mentioned.
example: 别对他要求太高，他毕竟才学了三个月。 (Bié duì tā yāoqiú tài gāo, tā bìjìng cái xué le sān gè yuè.)
example_translation: Don't demand too much of him; after all, he has only been studying for three months. / তার কাছে খুব বেশি আশা করো না, কারণ সে তো মাত্র তিন মাস ধরে শিখছে।

title: Sudden Realization 'No Wonder' with 怪不得
explanation: Use 怪不得 ('no wonder') at the start of a clause once you learn the hidden reason behind something that previously puzzled you.
example: 原来他昨晚没睡好，怪不得今天一直打哈欠。 (Yuánlái tā zuówǎn méi shuìhǎo, guàibudé jīntiān yīzhí dǎ hāqian.)
example_translation: So he didn't sleep well last night—no wonder he keeps yawning today. / আচ্ছা, সে গত রাতে ভালো ঘুমায়নি—তা-ই তো আজ সারাদিন হাই তুলছে।

title: Intense Wish with 恨不得 (hènbudé)
explanation: Place 恨不得 ('wish one could / dying to') before a verb phrase to express an eager, often exaggerated desire to do something impossible or immediate.
example: 好久没回家了，我恨不得立刻飞到父母身边。 (Hǎojiǔ méi huíjiā le, wǒ hènbudé lìkè fēi dào fùmǔ shēnbiān.)
example_translation: I haven't been home in so long that I wish I could fly to my parents' side immediately. / অনেক দিন বাড়ি যাইনি, ইচ্ছে করছে এক্ষুনি উড়ে বাবা-মায়ের কাছে চলে যাই।

title: Absolute Necessity with 非…不可
explanation: Frame a verb or noun phrase in 非…不可 ('must / have to / bound to') to convey unyielding determination or inevitability.
example: 这件事关系重大，我今天非搞清楚不可。 (Zhè jiàn shì guānxì zhòngdà, wǒ jīntiān fēi gǎo qīngchu bùkě.)
example_translation: This matter is of great importance; I simply must get to the bottom of it today. / বিষয়টি অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ, আজ আমাকে যেভাবেই হোক এটি পরিষ্কারভাবে জানতে হবে।

title: Hyperbolic Emphasis 'Simply' with 简直 (jiǎnzhí)
explanation: Use 简直 ('simply / virtually / downright') before an exaggeration or strong assessment to show something reaches an unbelievable degree.
example: 这儿的夜景简直像一幅油画一样美。 (Zhèr de yèjǐng jiǎnzhí xiàng yī fú yóuhuà yīyàng měi.)
example_translation: The night view here is simply as beautiful as an oil painting. / এখানকার রাতের দৃশ্য একেবারে একটি তৈলচিত্রের মতো সুন্দর।

title: Defining or Questioning 'So-Called' with 所谓
explanation: 所谓 ('so-called / what is called') modifies a noun to either formally define a term or cast skeptical quotation marks around it.
example: 所谓的“捷径”，往往隐藏着更大的风险。 (Suǒwèi de 'jiéjìng', wǎngwǎng yǐncáng zhe gèng dà de fēngxiǎn.)
example_translation: So-called 'shortcuts' often hide even greater risks. / তথাকথিত 'শর্টকাট'-এর আড়ালে প্রায়ই আরও বড় ঝুঁকি লুকিয়ে থাকে।

title: Shifting Topic 'As For' with 至于 (zhìyú)
explanation: 至于 ('as for / when it comes to') introduces a new, related subtopic in the second part of a discussion, often contrasting it with the first point.
example: 机票我已经订好了，至于酒店，明天再说吧。 (Jīpiào wǒ yǐjīng dìnghǎo le, zhìyú jiǔdiàn, míngtiān zài shuō ba.)
example_translation: I've already booked the flight; as for the hotel, let's discuss it tomorrow. / আমি ইতিমধ্যেই বিমানের টিকিট বুক করে ফেলেছি; আর হোটেলের ব্যাপারে আগামীকাল দেখা যাবে।

title: Drawing Evidence-Based Conclusions with 可见 (kějiàn)
explanation: 可见 ('from this it can be seen / thus it is clear') follows supporting evidence to state a logical deduction or conclusion.
example: 他连续五年获得第一名，可见平时有多么刻苦。 (Tā liánxù wǔ nián huòdé dì-yī míng, kějiàn píngshí yǒu duōme kèkǔ.)
example_translation: He won first place for five consecutive years, which shows how hardworking he usually is. / তিনি টানা পাঁচ বছর প্রথম স্থান অধিকার করেছেন, এ থেকেই বোঝা যায় তিনি সাধারণত কতটা পরিশ্রমী।

title: Repeatedly and Earnestly with 再三 (zàisān)
explanation: Place the adverb 再三 ('repeatedly / again and again') before a verb (such as 强调, 考虑, 请求) to convey deliberate, earnest repetition.
example: 教练再三叮嘱队员们赛前要注意休息。 (Jiàoliàn zàisān dīngzhǔ duìyuánmen sàiqián yào zhùyì xiūxi.)
example_translation: The coach repeatedly reminded the team members to be sure to rest before the match. / কোচ খেলোয়াড়দের খেলার আগে বিশ্রাম নেওয়ার জন্য বারবার সতর্ক করে দিলেন।

title: Universal Inclusion with 凡是 (fánshì)
explanation: 凡是 ('every / any / all who') introduces an all-inclusive scope at the start of a sentence and almost always pairs with 都 in the predicate.
example: 凡是参加本次活动的志愿者，都会获得证书。 (Fánshì cānjiā běncì huódòng de zhìyuànzhě, dōu huì huòdé zhèngshū.)
example_translation: Every volunteer who participates in this event will receive a certificate. / এই কার্যক্রমে অংশগ্রহণকারী প্রত্যেক স্বেচ্ছাসেবকই সনদপত্র পাবেন।

title: Reciprocity 'Each Other' with 彼此 (bǐcǐ)
explanation: 彼此 functions as a pronoun meaning 'each other / both parties' or as an adverb before verbs like 理解 and 尊重 to highlight mutual interaction.
example: 只有彼此信任，合作才能长久维持下去。 (Zhǐyǒu bǐcǐ xìnrèn, hézuò cái néng chángjiǔ wéichí xiàqù.)
example_translation: Only when both sides trust each other can cooperation be sustained in the long run. / কেবল পারস্পরিক বিশ্বাস থাকলেই সহযোগিতা দীর্ঘদিন টিকে থাকতে পারে।

pattern: 干干净净|高高兴兴|漂漂亮亮|清清楚楚
title: Adjective Reduplication (AABB) for Vivid Degree
explanation: Reduplicate two-syllable adjectives in the AABB pattern (e.g., 干净 → 干干净净, 清楚 → 清清楚楚) to intensify vividness or thoroughness without needing 很.
example: 她把房间收拾得干干净净的。 (Tā bǎ fángjiān shōushi de gāngānjìngjìng de.)
example_translation: She tidied up the room spotlessly clean. / সে ঘরটি একদম ঝকঝকে পরিষ্কার করে গুছিয়েছে।

title: Emphatic Rhetorical Questions (岂不是 / 难道…不成)
explanation: Use 岂不是 ('wouldn't that be...?') or 难道…不成 ('could it really be that...?') to challenge a claim forcefully in formal argument or sharp dialogue.
example: 如果不听劝告一意孤行，岂不是自找麻烦？ (Rúguǒ bù tīng quàngào yīyìgūxíng, qǐbúshì zìzhǎo máfan?)
example_translation: If you ignore advice and go your own way, wouldn't that be asking for trouble? / পরামর্শ না শুনে নিজের জেদে চললে কি নিজের বিপদ নিজেই ডেকে আনা হবে না?

title: Balanced Concession with 固然…但是/不过…
explanation: 固然 ('admittedly / to be sure') concedes that a point is true in the first clause, setting up a more important qualification introduced by 但是 or 不过.
example: 钱固然重要，但健康与家人的陪伴更加宝贵。 (Qián gùrán zhòngyào, dàn jiànkāng yǔ jiārén de péibàn gèngjiā bǎoguì.)
example_translation: Money is admittedly important, but health and the company of family are even more precious. / টাকা নিঃসন্দেহে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ, তবে স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবারের সান্নিধ্য আরও বেশি মূল্যবান।

title: Formal Escalation with 尚且…何况…
explanation: Pair 尚且 ('even') in the first clause with 何况 ('let alone / all the more') in the second to build a formal a fortiori argument.
example: 经验丰富的专家尚且会犯错，何况初学者呢？ (Jīngyàn fēngfù de zhuānjiā shàngqiě huì fàncuò, hékuàng chūxuézhě ne?)
example_translation: Even experienced experts make mistakes, let alone beginners! / অভিজ্ঞ বিশেষজ্ঞরাই যেখানে ভুল করেন, সেখানে নতুন শিক্ষার্থীদের কথা তো বলাই বাহুল্য!

title: Redefining Characterization with 与其说…不如说…
explanation: Use 与其说 + A + 不如说 + B ('rather than calling it A, it is more accurate to call it B') to refine how a situation is defined.
example: 这与其说是一次失败，不如说是一次宝贵的教训。 (Zhè yǔqí shuō shì yī cì shībài, bùrú shuō shì yī cì bǎoguì de jiàoxun.)
example_translation: Rather than calling this a failure, it is better described as a valuable lesson. / এটিকে ব্যর্থতা বলার চেয়ে বরং একটি মূল্যবান শিক্ষা বলাই ভালো।

title: Minimizing Scope 'Nothing More Than' with 无非
explanation: Place 无非 ('nothing more than / merely') before a verb phrase or 是 to narrow down motives or reasons to a simple core.
example: 他这么做，无非是想引起大家的注意罢了。 (Tā zhème zuò, wúfēi shì xiǎng yǐnqǐ dàjiā de zhùyì bàle.)
example_translation: By doing this, he merely wanted to attract everyone's attention. / সে এমনটা করেছে কেবল সবার দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ করার জন্যই।

title: Inevitability with 不免 (bùmiǎn) / 难免 (nánmiǎn)
explanation: 不免 ('inevitably / cannot help feeling') and 难免 ('hard to avoid') express that a reaction or flaw naturally occurs under given circumstances.
example: 初次上台演讲，心里难免会有些紧张。 (Chūcì shàngtái yǎnjiǎng, xīnlǐ nánmiǎn huì yǒuxiē jǐnzhāng.)
example_translation: When giving a speech on stage for the first time, it is hard to avoid feeling a bit nervous. / প্রথমবার মঞ্চে বক্তৃতা দেওয়ার সময় মনে কিছুটা নার্ভাসনেস আসা স্বাভাবিক।

title: Decisive Turning Point with 一旦…就…
explanation: Use 一旦 ('once / in the event that') paired with 就 to emphasize that crossing a threshold triggers an immediate or irreversible consequence.
example: 生态系统一旦遭到破坏，就很难在短期内恢复。 (Shēngtài xìtǒng yīdàn zāodào pòhuài, jiù hěn nán zài duǎnqī nèi huīfù.)
example_translation: Once an ecosystem is damaged, it is very difficult to restore in the short term. / বাস্তুতন্ত্র একবার ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হলে স্বল্প সময়ের মধ্যে তা পুনরুদ্ধার করা খুব কঠিন।

title: Formal Basis 'In View Of' with 鉴于 (jiànyú)
explanation: Begin a formal sentence or policy statement with 鉴于 + Fact/Situation ('in view of / given that') to justify an upcoming decision.
example: 鉴于近期天气变化剧烈，学校决定推迟运动会。 (Jiànyú jìnqī tiānqì biànhuà jùliè, xuéxiào juédìng tuīchí yùndònghuì.)
example_translation: In view of the drastic recent weather changes, the school decided to postpone the sports meet. / সাম্প্রতিক আবহাওয়ার তীব্র পরিবর্তনের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে স্কুল কর্তৃপক্ষ ক্রীড়া প্রতিযোগিতা স্থগিত করার সিদ্ধান্ত নিয়েছে।

title: Inverted Cause-Effect with 之所以…是因为…
explanation: State the result first with 之所以, then reveal the underlying reason with 是因为 ('the reason why [Result] is because [Cause]'). This places analytical focus on the explanation.
example: 他之所以能取得成功，是因为从不轻言放弃。 (Tā zhīsuǒyǐ néng qǔdé chénggōng, shì yīnwèi cóng bù qīngyán fàngqì.)
example_translation: The reason he was able to achieve success is that he never easily gave up. / তিনি যে সফল হতে পেরেছেন, তার কারণ হলো তিনি কখনোই সহজে হাল ছাড়েননি।

title: Present Simple: Habits & General Truths
explanation: Use the base verb for I/you/we/they and add -s/-es for he/she/it to describe routines, facts, and permanent states. Learners often forget the third-person singular -s ending in affirmative statements.
example: She drinks a cup of green tea every morning before work.
example_translation: সে প্রতিদিন কাজের আগে সকালে এক কাপ গ্রিন টি পান করে।

title: Basic Clause Word Order (SVO)
explanation: Standard English declarative sentences follow Subject + Verb + Object order, with place expressions usually coming before time expressions at the end. Avoid placing the verb before the subject in normal statements or splitting a verb from its direct object with an adverb.
example: They play football in the park every Friday afternoon.
example_translation: তারা প্রতি শুক্রবার বিকেলে পার্কে ফুটবল খেলে।

title: Verb 'to be' in the Present (am / is / are)
explanation: Use 'am' with I, 'is' with singular third-person subjects, and 'are' with you/we/they to express identity, states, locations, and ages. Unlike many languages, English never omits the linking verb 'to be' before adjectives or nouns.
example: My brother is a civil engineer, and my parents are retired.
example_translation: আমার ভাই একজন সিভিল ইঞ্জিনিয়ার, এবং আমার বাবা-মা অবসরপ্রাপ্ত।

title: Present Simple: Negatives & Questions (do / does)
explanation: Form Present Simple negatives with don't/doesn't + base verb and yes/no questions with Do/Does + subject + base verb. After 'does' or 'doesn't', always return the main verb to its base form without -s.
example: Does your sister work on Saturdays, or does she stay home?
example_translation: তোমার বোন কি শনিবারে কাজ করে, নাকি বাসায় থাকে?

title: Present Continuous (am/is/are + -ing)
explanation: Use am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening right now or temporary situations around the present time. Avoid using stative verbs like 'know', 'believe', or 'want' in continuous forms.
example: Please be quiet; the baby is sleeping in the next room right now.
example_translation: দয়া করে চুপ থাকুন; বাচ্চাটি এখন পাশের ঘরে ঘুমাচ্ছে।

title: Indefinite Articles (a / an)
explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds when introducing a singular countable noun for the first time. Choose between 'a' and 'an' by pronunciation, not spelling (e.g., 'an hour', 'a university').
example: He waited for an hour to buy a ticket at the station.
example_translation: সে স্টেশনে একটি টিকিট কিনতে এক ঘণ্টা অপেক্ষা করেছিল।

title: Definite Article (the)
explanation: Use 'the' before singular, plural, or uncountable nouns when both speaker and listener know the specific item, or when something is unique. Do not use 'the' when speaking about plural or uncountable nouns in general.
example: Could you close the window next to the door, please?
example_translation: দয়া করে দরজার পাশের জানালাটি কি বন্ধ করতে পারবেন?

title: Plural Nouns (Regular & Irregular)
explanation: Most English nouns take -s or -es in the plural, while common irregular nouns change form entirely (child -> children, person -> people). Never add -s to irregular plurals like 'children' or 'people'.
example: Many people bring their children to the museum on weekends.
example_translation: অনেক মানুষ সপ্তাহান্তে তাদের সন্তানদের জাদুঘরে নিয়ে আসে।

title: Subject & Object Pronouns
explanation: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they) before the verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them) after verbs or prepositions. A frequent error is using 'I' instead of 'me' after prepositions like 'between' or 'for'.
example: She called us yesterday and invited me to her birthday dinner.
example_translation: সে গতকাল আমাদের ফোন করেছিল এবং আমাকে তার জন্মদিনের রাতের খাবারে আমন্ত্রণ জানিয়েছিল।

title: Possessive Adjectives & Possessive 's
explanation: Use possessive adjectives (my, his, her, its, our, their) before nouns and add 's to singular nouns (or ' to regular plurals) to show ownership. Note that 'its' shows possession, whereas 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.
example: My friend's laptop is broken, so she is using her brother's tablet.
example_translation: আমার বন্ধুর ল্যাপটপ নষ্ট হয়ে গেছে, তাই সে তার ভাইয়ের ট্যাবলেট ব্যবহার করছে।

title: Demonstratives (this / that / these / those)
explanation: Use 'this' (singular) and 'these' (plural) for items near the speaker in space or time, and 'that' (singular) and 'those' (plural) for distant items. Always match singular or plural nouns and verbs to the demonstrative.
example: These shoes are comfortable, but those boots on the top shelf look warmer.
example_translation: এই জুতাগুলো আরামদায়ক, কিন্তু উপরের তাকের ওই বুটগুলো বেশি উষ্ণ মনে হচ্ছে।

title: Existence with 'There is / There are'
explanation: Use 'there is' with singular or uncountable nouns and 'there are' with plural nouns to state that something exists in a place. Avoid using 'it has' or 'they have' in place of 'there is/are'.
example: There is a pharmacy across the street, and there are two banks nearby.
example_translation: রাস্তার ওপারে একটি ফার্মেসি আছে, এবং কাছাকাছি দুটি ব্যাংক আছে।

title: Prepositions of Time (at / on / in)
explanation: Use 'at' for exact clock times and night, 'on' for specific days and dates, and 'in' for months, years, seasons, and parts of the day. Do not use a preposition before 'this', 'last', 'next', or 'every'.
example: The train leaves at 8:30 on Monday morning in October.
example_translation: ট্রেনটি অক্টোবরের সোমবার সকালে ৮:৩০ মিনিটে ছাড়ে।

title: Prepositions of Place (in / on / at / under / next to)
explanation: Use 'in' for enclosed spaces and cities/countries, 'on' for surfaces and streets, and 'at' for exact points or addresses. Specific spatial relations use prepositions like 'under', 'behind', 'between', and 'next to'.
example: The keys are on the kitchen table, right next to the fruit bowl.
example_translation: চাবিগুলো রান্নাঘরের টেবিলের উপর, ঠিক ফলের বাটির পাশেই আছে।

title: Modal 'can / can't' for Ability & Requests
explanation: Use 'can' or 'can't' followed by the bare infinitive (without 'to') to express present ability or make informal requests. Never add -s to 'can' for he/she/it or place 'to' after it.
example: She can speak three languages, but she cannot drive a car yet.
example_translation: সে তিনটি ভাষায় কথা বলতে পারে, কিন্তু এখনো গাড়ি চালাতে পারে না।

title: Adverbs of Frequency & Position
explanation: Adverbs like 'always', 'usually', 'often', 'sometimes', and 'never' go before the main verb, but after the verb 'to be'. Avoid using 'never' with another negative word like 'don't', which creates an unintended double negative.
example: He is always punctual, and he never misses a morning meeting.
example_translation: সে সবসময় সময়নিষ্ঠ, এবং কখনোই সকালের মিটিং মিস করে না।

title: Imperatives for Instructions & Advice
explanation: Use the base form of the verb without a subject to give commands, directions, or warnings, and add 'Don't' before the verb for negative imperatives. Add 'please' to make requests polite.
example: Turn left at the traffic light and don't forget to lock the gate.
example_translation: ট্রাফিক লাইটে বাম দিকে ঘুরুন এবং গেটে তালা দিতে ভুলবেন না।

title: Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns
explanation: Countable nouns have singular and plural forms and take 'a/an' or numbers, whereas uncountable nouns (information, advice, luggage, water) have no plural form and always take a singular verb. Never write 'informations' or 'an advice'; use 'a piece of advice' instead.
example: She gave me some useful advice and helpful information about the visa.
example_translation: সে আমাকে ভিসা সম্পর্কে কিছু দরকারি পরামর্শ ও সহায়ক তথ্য দিয়েছে।

title: Quantifiers: Some vs. Any
explanation: Use 'some' in affirmative sentences and polite offers/requests, and use 'any' in negative sentences and open questions with plural or uncountable nouns. Using 'some' in offers like 'Would you like some tea?' sounds warm and expects 'yes'.
example: We have some fresh bread, but we don't have any butter left.
example_translation: আমাদের কাছে কিছু তাজা রুটি আছে, কিন্তু কোনো মাখন অবশিষ্ট নেই।

title: Wh- Questions Word Order
explanation: Form Wh- questions with Question Word + Auxiliary (do/does/is/can) + Subject + Main Verb. When 'who' or 'what' is the subject of the question, do not add 'do' or 'does' (e.g., 'Who lives here?').
example: Where do you usually buy groceries when you finish work early?
example_translation: আপনি যখন তাড়াতাড়ি কাজ শেষ করেন, তখন সাধারণত কোথা থেকে বাজার করেন?

title: Past Simple: 'to be' (was / were)
explanation: Use 'was' with I/he/she/it and 'were' with you/we/they to describe completed past states, locations, and feelings. Form negatives with wasn't/weren't and questions by inverting was/were before the subject.
example: We were exhausted after the flight, and the hotel room was very quiet.
example_translation: ফ্লাইটের পর আমরা ভীষণ ক্লান্ত ছিলাম, আর হোটেলের ঘরটি খুব শান্ত ছিল।

title: Past Simple: Regular & Irregular Verbs
explanation: Use the Past Simple for finished actions at a specific past time, adding -ed to regular verbs or using the second form of irregular verbs. In negatives and questions with 'did' or 'didn't', always use the base verb.
example: Did you visit your grandparents last weekend, or did they come here?
example_translation: গত সপ্তাহান্তে তুমি কি দাদা-দাদির বাসায় গিয়েছিলে, নাকি তারা এখানে এসেছিলেন?

title: Past Continuous (was/were + -ing)
explanation: Use was/were + verb-ing for an action in progress at a specific moment in the past or as background when a shorter Past Simple event interrupted it. Typically pair 'while' with Past Continuous and 'when' with Past Simple.
example: I was cooking dinner when the power suddenly went out.
example_translation: আমি রাতের খাবার রান্না করছিলাম, তখন হঠাৎ বিদ্যুৎ চলে গেল।

title: Future Simple with 'will' (Predictions & Instant Decisions)
explanation: Use 'will' + base verb for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking, promises, offers, and general predictions. Avoid using 'will' after time words like 'when' or 'if' in future clauses.
example: That bag looks heavy—wait a second, I'll carry it upstairs for you.
example_translation: ব্যাগটা বেশ ভারী মনে হচ্ছে—একটু দাঁড়াও, আমি ওটা তোমার জন্য উপরে নিয়ে যাচ্ছি।

title: Future with 'be going to' (Plans & Evidence)
explanation: Use am/is/are + going to + base verb for prior plans and intentions, or for predictions based on visible present evidence. Learners often omit the auxiliary 'be' before 'going to'.
example: Look at those dark clouds; it is going to rain heavily soon.
example_translation: ওই কালো মেঘগুলোর দিকে তাকাও; শিগগিরই প্রবল বৃষ্টি হতে যাচ্ছে।

title: Present Continuous for Fixed Future Arrangements
explanation: Use the Present Continuous with a future time marker to talk about definite personal arrangements made with other people or booked in advance. Unlike 'going to', it implies the time and place are already settled.
example: I'm meeting Dr. Rahman at the clinic tomorrow afternoon at three.
example_translation: আমি আগামীকাল বিকেল তিনটায় ক্লিনিকে ড. রহমানের সাথে দেখা করছি।

title: Present Perfect Simple (have/has + Past Participle)
explanation: Use have/has + past participle for life experiences without a specific time, recent events with 'just', or past actions with a clear result now. Never pair Present Perfect with finished time expressions like 'yesterday' or 'in 2019'.
example: She has already sent the report, so you don't need to email it again.
example_translation: সে ইতিমধ্যেই প্রতিবেদনটি পাঠিয়ে দিয়েছে, তাই আপনার আর ইমেইল করার দরকার নেই।

title: Present Perfect with 'for' and 'since'
explanation: Use 'for' with a duration of time (for three years) and 'since' with a specific starting point (since 2021) to show states or actions continuing up to now. Do not use Present Simple instead of Present Perfect for duration up to the present.
example: They have lived in Sylhet for six years, since their youngest son was born.
example_translation: তারা তাদের ছোট ছেলের জন্মের পর থেকে ছয় বছর ধরে সিলেটে বসবাস করছে।

title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
explanation: Choose Past Simple when the time period is finished (yesterday, two days ago, last year) and Present Perfect when the time is unfinished or unspecified up to now. Watch out for 'Have you ever...?' followed by Past Simple details.
example: I have been to Cox's Bazar twice, and I went there last December.
example_translation: আমি দুবার কক্সবাজার গেছি, এবং গত ডিসেম্বরে সেখানে গিয়েছিলাম।

title: Quantifiers: Much / Many / A lot of
explanation: Use 'many' with plural countable nouns and 'much' with uncountable nouns, mainly in questions and negative sentences. In affirmative statements, 'a lot of' or 'lots of' sounds much more natural than 'much'.
example: We don't have much time left, though we still have a lot of tasks to finish.
example_translation: আমাদের হাতে আর বেশি সময় নেই, যদিও এখনো অনেক কাজ শেষ করা বাকি আছে।

title: Quantifiers: Few / A few / Little / A little
explanation: Use 'a few' (countable) and 'a little' (uncountable) to mean 'a small but sufficient amount', whereas 'few' and 'little' without 'a' carry a negative meaning of 'almost none'. Including or omitting 'a' completely changes the speaker's attitude.
example: Luckily, I have a few days off, though I have very little money for travel.
example_translation: সৌভাগ্যবশত আমার কয়েক দিন ছুটি আছে, যদিও ভ্রমণের জন্য আমার কাছে খুব কমই টাকা আছে।

title: Comparative Adjectives (-er / more ... than)
explanation: Add -er to short one-syllable adjectives (and two-syllable ones ending in -y) and use 'more' before longer adjectives, followed by 'than'. Never combine both forms (e.g., avoid 'more faster' or 'more better').
example: The coastal train is slower than the express bus, but it is much more comfortable.
example_translation: উপকূলীয় ট্রেনটি এক্সপ্রেস বাসের চেয়ে ধীরগতির, তবে এটি অনেক বেশি আরামদায়ক।

pattern: the most|the best|the worst|the least|the farthest
title: Superlative Adjectives (the -est / the most ...)
explanation: Use 'the' + adjective-est for short adjectives and 'the most' + adjective for longer ones to compare three or more items. Remember to use 'in' with places or groups ('the tallest in the class') rather than 'of'.
example: This is the quietest café in the neighborhood and serves the best espresso.
example_translation: এটি এলাকার সবচেয়ে নিরিবিলি ক্যাফে এবং এখানে সবচেয়ে ভালো এসপ্রেসো পরিবেশন করা হয়।

title: Prepositions of Movement
explanation: Use prepositions like 'to', 'into', 'onto', 'across', 'through', and 'along' after verbs of motion to show direction or path. Distinguish 'in' (static position) from 'into' (entering an enclosed space).
example: She walked across the bridge, went through the gate, and stepped into the garden.
example_translation: সে সেতু পার হয়ে হেঁটে গেল, গেট দিয়ে ঢুকল এবং বাগানে পা রাখল।

pattern: have to|has to|had to|don't have to|doesn't have to|didn't have to
title: Obligation & Lack of Necessity (have to / don't have to)
explanation: Use 'have to' for rules or external necessity, and 'don't/doesn't have to' when something is optional or unnecessary. Note that 'don't have to' means no obligation, NOT prohibition.
example: You have to wear a helmet on the site, but you don't have to bring your own boots.
example_translation: সাইটে আপনাকে অবশ্যই হেলমেট পরতে হবে, তবে নিজের বুট আনতে হবে না।

title: Strong Obligation & Prohibition (must / mustn't)
explanation: Use 'must' + base verb for strong personal obligation or official rules, and 'mustn't' to forbid an action completely. For past obligation, use 'had to' instead of 'must'.
example: Passengers must show a valid ID and mustn't leave luggage unattended.
example_translation: যাত্রীদের অবশ্যই বৈধ পরিচয়পত্র দেখাতে হবে এবং ব্যাগ অরক্ষিত অবস্থায় রাখা যাবে না।

title: Advice & Mild Obligation (should / ought to)
explanation: Use 'should' + base verb or 'ought to' + base verb to give advice, express what is right, or make gentle recommendations. Unlike 'ought to', 'should' never takes 'to' before the main verb.
example: You should back up your files tonight before updating the operating system.
example_translation: অপারেটিং সিস্টেম আপডেট করার আগে আজ রাতেই আপনার ফাইলগুলোর ব্যাকআপ রাখা উচিত।

title: Zero Article (General Concepts, Meals & Institutions)
explanation: Omit articles before plural or uncountable nouns used in a general sense, and before meals, languages, sports, and institutions like 'school', 'hospital', or 'bed' when referring to their primary purpose.
example: After breakfast, children go to school while adults travel to work.
example_translation: সকালের নাশতার পর শিশুরা স্কুলে যায় আর বড়রা কাজে যায়।

title: Possessive Pronouns (mine / yours / hers / theirs)
explanation: Possessive pronouns replace a possessive adjective plus noun (e.g., 'my phone' -> 'mine') and stand alone without a following noun. Never add an apostrophe to 'hers', 'ours', 'yours', or 'theirs'.
example: That umbrella isn't mine; I think it is hers because of the blue handle.
example_translation: ওই ছাতাটি আমার নয়; নীল হাতলের কারণে আমার মনে হয় ওটা ওর।

title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Indefinite Pronouns & Each/Every
explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone', 'someone', 'nobody', and nouns preceded by 'each' or 'every' always take a singular verb. Even when followed by 'of the' + plural noun ('each of the students'), the verb stays singular.
example: Everyone in the office knows that each of the computers needs an update.
example_translation: অফিসের সবাই জানে যে প্রতিটি কম্পিউটারেরই একটি আপডেট প্রয়োজন।

title: Present Perfect Continuous (have/has been + -ing)
explanation: Use have/has been + verb-ing to emphasize the duration or ongoing activity of an action that started in the past and continues now or just stopped with visible effects. For state verbs or completed quantities, use Present Perfect Simple instead.
example: She has been studying architecture for three years and looks tired lately.
example_translation: সে তিন বছর ধরে স্থাপত্যবিদ্যা পড়ছে এবং ইদানীং তাকে ক্লান্ত দেখাচ্ছে।

title: Past Perfect Simple (had + Past Participle)
explanation: Use had + past participle to show that one past action happened earlier than another past event in Past Simple. Avoid overusing Past Perfect when events are already stated in simple chronological order with 'and' or 'then'.
example: By the time we reached the cinema, the film had already started.
example_translation: আমরা সিনেমা হলে পৌঁছানোর আগেই ছবিটি শুরু হয়ে গিয়েছিল।

pattern: used to|didn't use to|did you use to
title: Past Habits & States (used to + Infinitive)
explanation: Use 'used to' + base verb for past habits or states that are no longer true today; use 'would' only for repeated past actions, never for states like 'live' or 'know'. In negatives and questions, drop the -d: 'didn't use to'.
example: I used to live near the river, and we would swim there every summer.
example_translation: আমি আগে নদীর কাছে থাকতাম, এবং প্রতি গ্রীষ্মে আমরা সেখানে সাঁতার কাটতাম।

pattern: be used to|am used to|is used to|are used to|get used to|getting used to
title: Familiarity & Adaptation (be/get used to + -ing / Noun)
explanation: Use 'be used to' for something already familiar and 'get used to' for the process of adapting to something new. Unlike 'used to + base verb', here 'to' is a preposition, so it must be followed by a noun or verb-ing.
example: After moving to Dhaka, he gradually got used to commuting in heavy traffic.
example_translation: ঢাকায় চলে আসার পর সে ধীরে ধীরে ভারী যানজটে যাতায়াত করতে অভ্যস্ত হয়ে উঠেছে।

title: Zero Conditional (General Truths & Scientific Facts)
explanation: Use 'If/When + Present Simple, Present Simple' for facts, natural laws, and habits that are always true whenever the condition happens. Here, 'if' and 'when' have almost the same meaning.
example: If you heat ice above zero degrees Celsius, it melts into water.
example_translation: আপনি যদি শূন্য ডিগ্রি সেলসিয়াসের উপরে বরফ গরম করেন, তবে তা গলে পানিতে পরিণত হয়।

title: First Conditional (Real Future Possibilities)
explanation: Use 'If + Present Simple, will/can/may + base verb' for likely future situations and their results. Never put 'will' inside the 'if' or 'unless' clause—always keep the condition clause in a present tense.
example: Unless you leave now, you will miss the last ferry across the river.
example_translation: আপনি যদি এখনই বের না হন, তবে নদী পার হওয়ার শেষ ফেরিটি মিস করবেন।

title: Second Conditional (Unreal Present or Future)
explanation: Use 'If + Past Simple, would/could/might + base verb' for imaginary, unlikely, or impossible situations in the present or future. In formal English, 'were' is preferred over 'was' for all subjects ('If I were you').
example: If I had more free time, I would learn to play the acoustic guitar.
example_translation: আমার হাতে যদি আরও অবসর সময় থাকত, তবে আমি অ্যাকোস্টিক গিটার বাজানো শিখতাম।

title: Passive Voice: Present & Past Simple
explanation: Form the passive with am/is/are or was/were + past participle when the action or receiver matters more than the doer, or when the doer is unknown. Introduce the agent with 'by' only when that information is important.
example: This bridge was built in 1998 and is inspected by engineers every year.
example_translation: এই সেতুটি ১৯৯৮ সালে নির্মিত হয়েছিল এবং প্রতি বছর প্রকৌশলীরা এটি পরিদর্শন করেন।

pattern: has been|have been|will be|can be|must be|should be
title: Passive Voice: Present Perfect & Modals
explanation: Use have/has been + past participle for passive Present Perfect, and modal + be + past participle for passive modals. Watch out for omitting 'been' or 'be', which turns the sentence into a broken active verb.
example: All the application forms have been reviewed, and the results will be emailed tomorrow.
example_translation: সব আবেদনপত্র পর্যালোচনা করা হয়েছে, এবং ফলাফল আগামীকাল ইমেইল করা হবে।

title: Defining Relative Clauses
explanation: Defining relative clauses identify which exact person, thing, or place we mean, using 'who/that' for people, 'which/that' for things, 'whose' for possession, and 'where' for places without commas. You may omit who/which/that only when it is the object of the relative clause.
example: The woman who designed our website works at the agency where my cousin interns.
example_translation: যে নারী আমাদের ওয়েবসাইটটি ডিজাইন করেছেন, তিনি সেই এজেন্সিতে কাজ করেন যেখানে আমার কাজিন ইন্টার্নশিপ করে।

title: Gerunds (-ing) as Subjects & After Verbs/Prepositions
explanation: Use verb-ing (a gerund) as the subject of a sentence, immediately after prepositions (without, before, interested in), and after verbs such as enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, and suggest. Avoid placing a to-infinitive directly after a preposition.
example: She suggested taking the metro instead of driving through the downtown traffic.
example_translation: শহরের যানজটের মধ্য দিয়ে গাড়ি চালানোর বদলে সে মেট্রোতে যাওয়ার পরামর্শ দিয়েছিল।

title: To-Infinitives After Verbs & Adjectives
explanation: Use to + base verb after verbs of intention or decision (decide, hope, plan, promise, refuse, manage) and after adjectives (easy to use, happy to help). Also use 'to + verb' to express purpose ('I came here to study').
example: He promised to send the contract today because it is important to finalize the deal.
example_translation: সে আজই চুক্তিপত্র পাঠানোর প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়েছে কারণ চুক্তিটি চূড়ান্ত করা জরুরি।

pattern: isn't it|aren't you|don't you|didn't he|won't you|can't she|haven't they|isn't he
title: Question Tags
explanation: Add a short auxiliary + pronoun tag at the end of a statement to confirm information: use a negative tag after a positive statement and a positive tag after a negative one. Note the irregular tag for 'I am': 'aren't I?'.
example: You have already booked the hotel room, haven't you?
example_translation: তুমি ইতিমধ্যেই হোটেলের ঘর বুক করেছ, তাই না?

title: Reflexive & Reciprocal Pronouns
explanation: Use reflexive pronouns (myself, themselves) when the subject and object are the same person, or for emphasis; use 'each other / one another' when two or more people do the action mutually. Do not confuse 'themselves' (self-directed) with 'each other' (mutual).
example: They blamed themselves for the mistake, yet they still supported each other.
example_translation: ভুলের জন্য তারা নিজেদের দোষারোপ করেছিল, তবুও তারা একে অপরকে সমর্থন করে গেছে।

title: Adverbs of Manner & Degree
explanation: Adverbs of manner describe how an action happens (usually -ly, plus irregular 'well', 'fast', 'hard') and go after the verb or object, while degree adverbs (quite, fairly, extremely) modify adjectives or other adverbs. Note that 'hardly' means 'almost not', not 'with effort'.
example: She spoke very clearly during the presentation and handled tough questions remarkably well.
example_translation: উপস্থাপনার সময় সে খুব স্পষ্টভাবে কথা বলেছে এবং কঠিন প্রশ্নগুলো দারুণভাবে সামলেছে।

title: Order of Adjectives Before a Noun
explanation: When multiple adjectives precede a noun, they generally follow the order: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material, Purpose (OSASCOMP). Avoid stringing more than three adjectives before one noun in natural writing.
example: They bought a lovely small antique round wooden dining table.
example_translation: তারা একটি সুন্দর ছোট প্রাচীন গোল কাঠের ডাইনিং টেবিল কিনেছে।

title: Equal & Unequal Comparisons (as ... as)
explanation: Use 'as + base adjective/adverb + as' to show equality and 'not as/so + adjective/adverb + as' to show a lesser degree. Always use the base form of the adjective between 'as ... as', never a comparative.
example: This new tablet is not as expensive as the laptop, and it works just as fast.
example_translation: এই নতুন ট্যাবলেটটি ল্যাপটপের মতো এত দামি নয়, এবং এটি ঠিক ততটাই দ্রুত কাজ করে।

title: Degree with 'Too' and 'Enough'
explanation: Place 'too' before adjectives/adverbs to mean 'more than wanted or needed', and place 'enough' AFTER adjectives/adverbs but BEFORE nouns. Avoid confusing 'too much' (excess) with 'very' (high degree).
example: The suitcase is too heavy to carry upstairs, and I am not strong enough to lift it.
example_translation: স্যুটকেসটি উপরে নিয়ে যাওয়ার জন্য অতিরিক্ত ভারী, আর আমি এটি তোলার মতো যথেষ্ট শক্তিশালী নই।

pattern: turn on|turn off|pick up|look after|give up|put off|find out|run out of
title: Phrasal Verbs: Separable vs. Inseparable
explanation: With separable phrasal verbs (pick up, turn off, put off), a noun object can go before or after the particle, whereas a pronoun object (it, them) MUST go between the verb and particle. Inseparable phrasal verbs (look after, run into) never split.
example: Please pick up the parcel from the desk, or ask Sam to pick it up before five.
example_translation: দয়া করে ডেস্ক থেকে পার্সেলটি তুলে নিন, অথবা পাঁচটার আগে স্যামকে ওটা তুলে নিতে বলুন।

pattern: may|could|would you mind|do you mind|be allowed to
title: Modals of Permission & Polite Requests
explanation: Use 'Can/Could/May I...?' to ask permission and 'Would you mind + -ing?' for very polite requests. Note that answering 'No, not at all' to 'Would you mind...?' means you agree to do it.
example: Could I borrow your charger for ten minutes, or would you mind lending me the power bank?
example_translation: আমি কি দশ মিনিটের জন্য আপনার চার্জারটি ধার নিতে পারি, নাকি আপনার পাওয়ার ব্যাংকটি ধার দিতে আপত্তি হবে?

title: Reported Speech: Statements & Tense Backshift
explanation: When reporting past statements with 'said (that)' or 'told someone (that)', shift tenses one step back (Present Simple -> Past Simple, will -> would) and adjust pronouns and time words. Remember that 'tell' requires a personal object ('told me'), whereas 'say' does not.
example: Nadia told me that she was moving to Chattogram the following month.
example_translation: নাদিয়া আমাকে বলেছিল যে সে পরের মাসে চট্টগ্রামে চলে যাচ্ছে।

title: Reported Speech: Questions & Commands
explanation: Report yes/no questions with 'asked + if/whether' and Wh- questions with the question word, using statement word order (subject before verb) without 'do/did'. Report commands with 'told/asked + object + (not) to + verb'.
example: The guard asked us where we were going and told us not to take photos inside.
example_translation: প্রহরী আমাদের জিজ্ঞেস করেছিলেন আমরা কোথায় যাচ্ছি এবং ভেতরে ছবি না তুলতে বলেছিলেন।

title: Correlative Conjunctions: Both / Neither / Either
explanation: Use 'both A and B' with a plural verb for two items together; use 'either A or B' and 'neither A nor B' with a verb that agrees with the closer subject B. Avoid using 'neither' with a negative verb like 'didn't'.
example: Neither the manager nor the assistants were informed about the schedule change.
example_translation: সময়সূচী পরিবর্তনের বিষয়ে ব্যবস্থাপক বা সহকারীরা কেউই অবগত ছিলেন না।

title: Clauses of Contrast (although / even though / however)
explanation: Use 'although', 'though', or 'even though' followed by a full subject + verb clause, and never put 'but' after an 'although' clause in the same sentence. 'However' is a conjunctive adverb that connects separate sentences or clauses with a semicolon and comma.
example: Even though the hike was exhausting, the view from the summit was worth every step.
example_translation: হাইকিংটি ক্লান্তিকর হলেও চূড়া থেকে দৃশ্যটি প্রতিটি পদক্ষেপের যোগ্য ছিল।

title: Prepositions of Contrast (despite / in spite of)
explanation: Follow 'despite' or 'in spite of' with a noun phrase, pronoun, or gerund (-ing), never directly with a subject + finite verb clause. To introduce a clause, add 'the fact that' (e.g., 'despite the fact that it rained'). Never write 'despite of'.
example: Despite having a slight fever, Tariq delivered a confident keynote speech.
example_translation: সামান্য জ্বর থাকা সত্ত্বেও তারিক আত্মবিশ্বাসের সাথে মূল বক্তব্য প্রদান করেছে।

title: Past Perfect Continuous (had been + -ing)
explanation: Use had been + verb-ing to emphasize how long an action had been continuing before a specific moment or event in the past, or to explain a past result. Like other continuous tenses, it is rarely used with stative verbs.
example: Her eyes were red because she had been staring at the screen for six hours.
example_translation: তার চোখ লাল হয়ে ছিল কারণ সে ছয় ঘণ্টা ধরে একটানা স্ক্রিনের দিকে তাকিয়ে ছিল।

pattern: will be|'ll be|this time tomorrow|at 5 pm
title: Future Continuous (will be + -ing)
explanation: Use will be + verb-ing for an action that will be in progress at a specific moment in the future, or to ask politely about someone's existing plans. It avoids sounding pushy when inquiring about schedules.
example: This time tomorrow, we will be flying over the Bay of Bengal on our way to Bangkok.
example_translation: আগামীকাল এই সময়ে আমরা ব্যাংককের পথে বঙ্গোপসাগরের উপর দিয়ে উড়ে যাচ্ছি হব।

pattern: will have|'ll have|by|by the time|by next
title: Future Perfect Simple (will have + Past Participle)
explanation: Use will have + past participle to describe an action that will be completed before a specific deadline or event in the future. It commonly pairs with 'by + time' or 'by the time + Present Simple'.
example: By the time the guests arrive, we will have finished decorating the hall.
example_translation: অতিথিরা পৌঁছানোর আগেই আমরা হলঘর সাজানো শেষ করে ফেলব।

title: Future Perfect Continuous (will have been + -ing)
explanation: Use will have been + verb-ing to emphasize the total duration of an ongoing activity up to a future point in time. Both 'by' (the future endpoint) and 'for' (the duration) usually appear in the sentence.
example: By next July, Professor Karim will have been teaching at this university for twenty years.
example_translation: আগামী জুলাই নাগাদ অধ্যাপক করিম এই বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে বিশ বছর ধরে শিক্ষকতা করে আসছেন হবেন।

title: Third Conditional (Unreal Past & Regrets)
explanation: Use 'If + Past Perfect (had + past participle), would/could/might have + past participle' to imagine how a different past action would have changed a past result. Never put 'would have' inside the 'if' clause.
example: If you had checked the weather forecast, you would have packed a raincoat.
example_translation: আপনি যদি আবহাওয়ার পূর্বাভাস দেখে নিতেন, তবে একটি রেইনকোট সঙ্গে নিতেন।

title: Mixed Conditionals (Past Cause -> Present Result)
explanation: Combine a Third Conditional 'if' clause (If + Past Perfect) with a Second Conditional main clause (would + base verb) to link an unreal past event to a present consequence, or vice versa for ongoing traits affecting past outcomes.
example: If she had accepted that scholarship in 2020, she would be working in Zurich now.
example_translation: সে যদি ২০২০ সালে ওই বৃত্তিটি গ্রহণ করত, তবে এখন জুরিখে কাজ করত।

title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses
explanation: Set off non-defining relative clauses with commas to add extra, non-essential information about an already identified noun. Never use 'that' instead of 'who' or 'which', and never omit the relative pronoun.
example: My laptop, which I bought only six months ago, already needs a new battery.
